stem: Two candidate parents express a similar target phenotype, but progeny from one candidate are much more consistent across repeated evaluations. Which candidate provides stronger evidence for selection toward stability?
choices: The candidate with more repeatable progeny performance aligned with the breeding objective.
The candidate with the tallest single offspring regardless of the rest of the progeny.
Both are equally supported because the parents looked similar.
rationale: Repeatable progeny performance provides stronger evidence about transmissible trait stability than a parent's phenotype alone.
